Render a reproducible survey report

Source: R/reporting.R
render_report.Rd

Generates an HTML report that includes the instrument codebook, data quality summary, reliability diagnostics, and analysis-plan content. Quarto is the report engine. Without Quarto, surveyframe writes a short plain results page with the numbers, tables, charts and APA result lines, under a banner that links to the Quarto installation page. That page gets no new features and is not promised to match the Quarto report.

Usage

render_report(
  instrument,
  data = NULL,
  output_file = NULL,
  output_path = NULL,
  format = c("html", "pdf", "docx", "odt", "qmd"),
  include_quality = TRUE,
  include_reliability = TRUE,
  include_codebook = TRUE,
  include_missing = TRUE,
  include_descriptives = TRUE,
  include_analysis = TRUE,
  include_models = TRUE,
  plot_palette = c("web", "print"),
  interpretations = NULL,
  show_code = TRUE,
  references = NULL,
  csl = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  authors = NULL,
  figures = getOption("surveyframe.figures"),
  figure_dir = NULL,
  open = interactive()
)

Arguments

instrument

An sframe object.

data

A tibble or data.frame of responses, or NULL to generate a codebook-only report.

output_file

Character or NULL. The output file path. When NULL, a temporary file is written and its path returned.

output_path

Character or NULL. Alias for output_file. If both are supplied, output_file takes precedence.

format

Character. Output format: "html" (default), "pdf", "docx" (Word), "odt" (OpenDocument) or "qmd" (the Quarto source). Word and OpenDocument go through Quarto, styled by bundled APA 7 reference documents (Times New Roman 12, double spacing, APA headings), and stop with a message when Quarto is not found. PDF goes through Quarto and LaTeX when a LaTeX engine is found (TinyTeX, or xelatex, lualatex or pdflatex on the PATH), through the Typst Quarto bundles otherwise, and without Quarto prints the built-in HTML page through pagedown::chrome_print(), which needs the pagedown package (in Suggests) and a local Chrome or Chromium. The returned path's "converter" attribute names the route: "quarto-latex", "quarto-typst", "pagedown", or "quarto" for Word and OpenDocument. Every route renders offline. "qmd" writes the Quarto source of the report as a folder, named by output_file (a trailing .qmd is dropped), which must be new or empty: report.qmd, the .sframe, responses.csv, the bibliography and its style, the results record and manifest.json, and no _quarto.yml. Open report.qmd in RStudio or Positron and render it. It recomputes every number from the folder's files and checks them, through sframe_report_source(). Writing the folder needs no Quarto.

include_quality

Logical. Whether to include the data quality report. Requires data. Defaults to TRUE.

include_reliability

Logical. Whether to include reliability diagnostics. Requires data. Defaults to TRUE.

include_codebook

Logical. Whether to include the instrument codebook. Defaults to TRUE.

include_missing

Logical. Whether to include the missing-data report. Requires data. Defaults to TRUE.

include_descriptives

Logical. Whether to include descriptive statistics. Requires data. Defaults to TRUE.

include_analysis

Logical. Whether to include analysis-plan results when data are supplied and the instrument has an analysis_plan.

include_models

Logical. Whether to include saved model JSON and generated syntax blocks. Defaults to TRUE.

plot_palette

One of "web" (brand colours, for on-screen reading) or "print" (black, grey, and white, for a journal-ready or print-friendly report). Applied to every chart the report embeds. See sframe_brand().

interpretations

Named list or NULL. Written interpretations keyed by analysis-plan block id, added after the results are known. Each block's section prints the hypotheses and planned decision rule it declared before its result, with or without an entry. An entry prints after the result under "Interpretation (written after the results)", in place of any interpretation the block holds. Interpretations are report content only and are never written into the instrument.

show_code

Logical. Whether each result carries a folded "Show R code" block with the statistical call that produced it, built by sframe_syntax_result() from the same resolved specification the analysis ran. Defaults to TRUE. A method sframe_syntax_result() does not cover shows no block, rather than a guess at the call.

references

Optional further sframe_reference() records, for example the works a host cites in the written interpretations, which are cited in text as [@id]. The instrument's own references (sframe_add_references()) and the methods' references are always included.

csl

The citation style of the references: a bundled style name, "apa" (APA 7, the default), "chicago-author-date", "harvard" (Cite Them Right), "ieee" or "mla", or the path to a Citation Style Language (.csl) file, such as one saved from https://www.zotero.org/styles. Styles are never fetched from the network. The style's name and sha256 go into the results record and the manifest, and a .qmd report folder holds a copy named for it, so a rerun uses that copy. The built-in engine formats APA 7 only and says so when another style is asked for. An unknown name stops with the list of the 5.

title

Character or NULL. The report's title. Defaults to the instrument's title.

authors

Character vector or NULL. The report's authors, shown under the title. Defaults to the instrument's authors, and is left out when there are none.

figures

List or NULL. Size, resolution and format for every figure in the report: any of width and height in inches, dpi, and format, "png" or "svg" inside the report. For example list(width = 6.5, height = 4, dpi = 300). Absent entries keep each engine's own default. Defaults to the surveyframe.figures option, so a host can set it once with options(surveyframe.figures = list(dpi = 300)).

figure_dir

Character or NULL. A directory to write each analysis plan chart into as its own file, through sframe_save_figures(), at the size, resolution and format in figures, where format may also be "tiff", "jpeg" or "pdf". Needs data. Defaults to 300 dpi at 7 by 4.5 inches where figures names none.

open

Logical. Whether to show the finished report: in the viewer pane of RStudio, Positron or VS Code, and in the web browser otherwise. Defaults to TRUE in an interactive session and FALSE in a script. Nothing opens during a knitr or Quarto render.

Value

The output file path, invisibly.

Which Quarto

The first copy of Quarto that runs quarto --version is used, searched in this order: the executable named by the QUARTO_PATH environment variable, quarto on the PATH, RSTUDIO_QUARTO (set inside RStudio), the copy bundled with RStudio, then the copy bundled with Positron. RStudio and Positron do not put their copies on the PATH, so a report rendered outside them found none before 0.4.3. QUARTO_PATH takes the path of the executable itself, as in the quarto package. The Quarto report gives the version used and where it was found, and the returned path carries the executable as its "quarto" attribute. options(surveyframe.use_quarto = FALSE) uses the built-in engine whatever is installed.

Markdown in text fields

A research question, H0, H1, decision rule, interpretation, study problem or deviation report may hold Markdown: bold, italic, bulleted and numbered lists, links, [@key] citations, ~sub~, ^sup^, footnotes ^[...] and equations, $...$ inline and $$...$$ display (an opening $ needs a non-space on its right and a closing $ a non-space on its left and no digit after it, so "costs $5 and $10" stays prose). The .sframe keeps the text as typed. The Quarto report renders it, with equations as MathML, which needs no script or network. The built-in page renders it with commonmark and prints each equation's TeX in monospace. Shortcodes, raw blocks, ::: fences, heading lines, a --- line and HTML tags print as typed, R code in a field is never run, and @word is a citation only when word is the key of a reference the report holds.

Results record, manifest and provenance

Beside every report render_report() writes 2 files named after it. For report.html they are report_results.json, the plan results as canonical JSON (sorted keys, full precision, no timestamp, so the same instrument and responses give the same file), and report_manifest.json, the sha256 of the instrument content, the responses, the results record and the report as generated, with the surveyframe and R versions and the time. A report edited later, as a Word copy is meant to be, no longer matches its recorded hash, while the results record still does. The Provenance section at the top of the report gives the instrument hash and whether read_sframe() verified it, the number of amendments, the responses sha256 and the results record's sha256. The responses are hashed as JSON by column, so the hash belongs to the values, not to a file.

References

The Quarto report cites in text, author and year, and lists every work it cites once, in a References section at the end, formatted by pandoc's citation processor in the chosen style. That covers the methods' own references, the sources the instrument cites for its items, scales, plan blocks and models, and references. The built-in HTML engine, used when Quarto is unavailable, lists the methods' references the same way.

See also

sframe_codebook(), sframe_quality_results(), sframe_reliability_results()

Examples

instr <- read_sframe(
  system.file("extdata", "tourism_services_demo.sframe",
              package = "surveyframe")
)
responses <- read_responses(
  system.file("extdata", "tourism_services_responses.csv",
              package = "surveyframe"),
  instr,
  respondent_id = "respondent_id",
  submitted_at = "submitted_at",
  meta_cols = "started_at"
)
# \donttest{
old <- options(surveyframe.use_quarto = FALSE)
out <- tryCatch(
  render_report(
    instr,
    data = responses,
    output_file = tempfile(fileext = ".html"),
    include_reliability = FALSE,
    include_analysis = FALSE
  ),
  finally = options(old)
)
#> Report rendered with the built-in HTML engine: /tmp/RtmpEPGRzn/file1fca3998ade9.html
file.exists(out)
#> [1] TRUE
# }
